finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-1] Middleware lets protected routes bypass on misconfig/error
File: src/middleware.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: The middleware returns NextResponse.next() if process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is missing and also returns NextResponse.next() in the outer catch(), effectively allowing all requests to proceed when Clerk is misconfigured or the middleware throws. This directly bypasses the auth gate (auth.protect()) for /admin and /api/admin routes.  
Impact: Admin and API protection can be disabled by a misconfigured env or transient middleware error, exposing sensitive admin surfaces at any scale.  
Fix: Fail closed: return 401/redirect for protected routes when Clerk is not configured or when middleware errors, and log/alert the deployment instead of allowing NextResponse.next().

[AUTH-2] Missing DB index on provider ID causes full-table scans
File: prisma/schema.prisma (User model) (L12-L28)
Evidence: User model declares clerkId String? with no @unique or @@index, while server code performs prisma.user.findFirst({ where: { clerkId: userId } }) on every protected/admin request (e.g., src/app/api/admin/*).  
Impact: Each admin-auth lookup will trigger full table scans as user count grows, causing DB CPU and latency storms on auth-protected endpoints under load, leading to outages.  
Fix: Add an index or unique constraint on clerkId (e.g., clerkId String? @unique or @@index([clerkId])), create a migration, and backfill existing rows.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-3] Per-request DB mapping of clerkId -> email with no cache
File: src/app/api/admin/check-admin/route.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: After auth(), handlers always run prisma.user.findFirst({ where: { clerkId: userId }, select: { email: true } }) to resolve user email for authorization.  
Impact: Even with an index, auth checks hit the primary DB on every admin request (and multiple admin endpoints), becoming a hot path under scale; missing caching makes the DB the single auth hotspot.  
Fix: Cache clerkId→email mappings in a fast store (Redis) or derive/attach the email to the request/session token (or use Clerk server-side SDK to fetch only when missing).

[AUTH-4] Clerk webhook user-create lacks idempotent upsert handling
File: src/app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: handleUserCreated() does prisma.user.findUnique(...) then conditionally prisma.user.create(...) or prisma.user.update(...); it does not upsert on create path and can race/duplicate on concurrent/retried events (while handleUserUpdated uses upsert).  
Impact: Under concurrent webhook delivery or Clerk retries, this can produce unique-constraint errors or failed webhook handling (500), causing missed user-syncs and inconsistent clerkId mapping.  
Fix: Use a single atomic upsert keyed on a unique column (make clerkId or email unique/indexed) or deduplicate incoming events and return 2xx for already-applied events.

--- INFO ---

[AUTH-5] Provider and session model
File: package.json / src/ (project context)
Evidence: Repository uses @clerk/nextjs with Next.js App Router; sessions are provider-managed by Clerk (no local session table).
